This implies a potential mechanism of action involving the interaction of phenothiazines with Htr2a, possibly through a common binding site or pathway. The low common ancestor between Thioproperazine and Pipotiazine further supports a shared pharmacological profile, reinforcing the likelihood of a mechanistic link. The presence of a binding interaction between Pipotiazine and Htr2a, coupled with the structural similarities among the related compounds, suggests that Thioproperazine may also exert a similar effect on Htr2a. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible role for phenothiazines in modulating Htr2a activity, though further experimental validation is required to confirm this relationship.
